channel.title: SCC Online Web Edition - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from SCC Online Web Edition (scconline.com)

item.title: Punjab and Haryana High Court stays proceedings against Guru Randhawa over alleged outraging of religious feelings
item.description: Punjab and Haryana High Court: Guru Randhawa gets relief as HC stays proceedings in case over alleged outraging of religious feelings.

item.title: Call for Participation | CCCPL RGNUL to organise an International Conference on "Expanding Horizons of Consumer Law in the Age of Globalisation."
item.description: Rajiv Gandhi National University of Law hosts an international conference on consumer law, digital markets, and globalisation on April 5-6, 2026.

item.title: Strained marriage and alcohol addiction not enough to presume husband's guilt in wife's murder: Madras HC
item.description: Madras High Court sets aside conviction of a husband under Section 302 IPC for the alleged murder of his wife, holding that alcohol addiction and strained marriage cannot be treated as proof of a wife's murder.

item.title: Explained | Why Delhi High Court injuncted Smotect's misleading surrogate ads targeting "Vimal Elaichi"
item.description: Delhi High Court grants injunction against misleading ads portraying Vimal Elaichi as a tobacco product. Read how the Court addressed surrogate advertising, disparagement, and copyright infringement.

item.title: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas represented a consortium of lenders comprising of MUFG Bank, Ltd and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Gift City Branch
item.description: Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas advised MUFG Bank and SMBC on ECB financing for Adani Energy's 6000 MW HVDC transmission project.

item.title: Bombay High Court explains when Principal Seat continues to retain Jurisdiction despite Establishment of a Circuit Bench
item.description: Bombay High Court explains the Principal Seat's jurisdiction upon the establishment of a Circuit Bench, clarifying why pending matters do not automatically transfer

item.title: Relaxation in qualifying exam doesn't bar reserved category candidates' migration to open category on merit unless expressly prohibited: Supreme Court
item.description: Supreme Court holds that relaxation in a qualifying examination only affects eligibility and does not prevent reserved category candidates' migration to open category on merit unless recruitment rules expressly prohibit such migration.

item.title: Delhi High Court directs Registrar General to consider formulation of Child Access and Custody Guidelines with Parenting Plan
item.description: Delhi High Court directs its Registrar General to consider formulation of Child Access and Custody Guidelines with Parenting Plan.

item.title: Offshore Structures and India’s Insolvency Framework: Navigating Cross-Border Restructuring Complexities
item.description: Explore how offshore jurisdictions like BVI interact with India’s Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. Expert insights on cross-border restructuring, creditor rights, and legal coordination.

item.title: ‘Subjected to structural disadvantages’; SC flags systemic unfairness for women in Armed Forces over consideration of SSCWOs for Permanent Commission
item.description: ‘Subjected to structural disadvantages’; SC flags systemic unfairness for women in Armed Forces over consideration of SSCWOs for Permanent Commission.
